title: A folder deleted during the scan is noted as gone, not listed as unreadable
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: Assert.True failure: a folder deleted after its parent was listed and before the walk opened it was recorded as unreadable: C:\Users\sshub\AppData\Local\Temp\taad3-runs\c5430\fsa-tests\89223b3578a3489182ea57806a4d5e84\z (error 2, NothingListed).
A folder whose open fails with ERROR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (2) after its parent was listed is not flagged EntryFlags.Unreadable and is not added to ScanResult.Unreadable: missing
A folder whose open fails with ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND (3) because its parent was deleted too is likewise not flagged Unreadable or recorded in ScanResult.Unreadable: missing
Vanished folders are counted in a new ScanResult count (FoldersVanished or equivalent): missing
The scan's outcome notes carry a note for vanished folders, like the VanishedBeforeProbe note for files: missing
The vanished folder's top-level row finishes as an empty folder, not as Unreadable ('could not be opened') or as 'N folders inside could not be read': missing
The live 'N folders unreadable' counter does not count a vanished folder: missing
The 'Unreadable folders (N)' tab does not list a vanished folder as 'could not be opened': missing
The largest-files and kinds captions do not say files in a vanished folder 'may be missing': missing
combined-gone-fixes-leave-only-refused: Leaves only r, FoldersVanished 4, but 1 of 413 base-passing tests fails (cancel-guard rule)

Count only, no per-folder mark: the folder tree and the results list show a vanished folder as a plain empty folder, and only the ending's note says folders were deleted, as the file note does. A reviewer may want the tree to say which folders went. That needs a list of entries on ScanResult (additive) and tree wording.
Note wording: 'deleted while the scan ran, before it could be read; it is counted as an empty folder' against something shorter such as 'N folders were deleted during the scan'.
Where FolderVanished lives: in Scanner beside FailedKind (chosen, because it reads the walk's phase) or in SizeProbe beside IsGone.
Delete-pending folders (open fails with 5) and folders replaced by a file (listing 87) stay unreadable, as the design decided. The NTSTATUS split and the handle check are not built.
No per-folder 'deleted' mark in the folder tree or results list and no live 'deleted' counter: only the ending's count and note, as designed.

Exit codes 2 and 70 and the throw-mode, missing-value and unwritable-path runs are not re-checked in the new window script; review M2's prescription left them to the existing cases. This script checks exit 0 and the schema-1 keys.

At a finished ending the outcome texts are capped at 76 px while the tabs show (measured here: actualHeight 76, extentHeight 97.12), so the new note, like the files-vanished and probe-failure notes, can sit a scroll away. The layout is not this slice's. It is worth its own slice if the notes should be seen without scrolling.

Check on an SMB share (the loopback rig), a DFS link whose target is down, ReFS and FAT/exFAT that a queued folder deleted mid-scan reaches core.foldersVanished and that a folder still there but unreachable never does. This is the design's filed item for a person and O-002. The root check makes a dropped share stay unreadable, but its codes were measured only on SUBST and local NTFS.
W-001 and W-003 verdicts do not read the ending's notes (review M1's remark). A cut share now keeps its unreadable rows, but a later slice could have Get-ShareVerdict read the notes.

Ending text and the walk changed under src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning and src/FsAnalyser.App, so the C:\ and OneDrive proof runs and the network pass go stale under the project's rule. The runs come after E-007, E-006 and E-005 per Q-016, so this changes nothing about their order.

deviation: Review M1's critic prescribed that an aborted root check stamps nothing and counts nothing and that FolderDone's final return then ends the scan Cancelled. I return from FolderDone before SetChildren in that case, so the folder stays NotListed as any Stop-cut folder does, not listed-empty. This keeps the established rule that an aborted call commits nothing. VanishedFolderTests.AStopInTheRootCheckStampsNothingAndCountsNothing pins it for a cancel before and during the call.

deviation: Review M1 offered a [Collection] with DisableParallelization or a retry for the SUBST race. I took neither: SubstDrive is one shared helper whose letter pick and subst.exe call run under a static lock. All test classes run in one process, so the lock closes the race without serialising ContainerLayerStoreTests with the rest of the suite.

deviation: The design's FolderVanished(error, opened) is as specified; the root check is a second pure predicate, GoneGivenRootOpen(rootOpenError), and RootOpenError() in Run. The design did not have them; review M1 required the root check.

deviation: No workaround checkbox or KnownWorkarounds entry: the classification is this project's own, and the root check guards against the OS answering 2 or 3 for a path that stopped resolving, which is the app's own heuristic. Nothing outside the project is worked around.

deviation: The design's planted E007* finish-line tests do not exist in the tree (lessons #876, #888, #896). Review M2 handed their cases to the builder, so the material checks are VanishedFolderTests and tests/window/SL-005-VanishedFolders.Tests.ps1.

critique missed: The critique found that 2 and 3 can mean the volume, letter or share was lost (M1), but did not ask whether renaming or moving a queued folder, or any folder between it and the root, also gives 2 or 3 while the root still opens. Probe: Directory.Move(z, moved) at AfterFolder n==1 gave FoldersVanished 1, Unreadable 0 and the 4,096-byte file still on disk. The ending says 'deleted' and drops the 'may be missing' captions, which is the harm M1 was rated major for, on a narrower scope. A check: move a queued folder at AfterFolder n==1 and assert it is not counted deleted. Waived as N-055 and N-056.

critique missed: The critique's m1 fix (add `error\s*(?:==|is)\s*[23]`, widen the case pattern) was followed and still let `case 2 or 3:`, `case (2 or 3):`, `case 3 or 2:` and the `2 or 3 =>` / `{ 2 => true, 3 => true }` switch-arm spellings through. The critic's own check of the fix noticed `error is (2 or 3)` and called such gaps acceptable tripwire gaps. This codebase already writes `is A or B` (SizeProbe.IsGone, Scanner.ListRoot ~:303), so the next spelling was foreseeable. A check: run the rule's patterns over the C# 9 combinator spellings, or sweep FolderVanished over all error codes.

critique missed: The design checked the new ending note only through report-mode OutcomeNotes.lines and never asked whether the note is visible. OutcomeTexts is capped at 76 px and Q-002 was already open on that cap. The new note is the 4th of 4 on a live C:\ and the content is 160.96 px high. A check: assert the note's line is inside the visible 76 px, or that Q-002 is settled first.

still unknown: Does the root check stall on a cut network share? Every queued folder that fails with 2 or 3 re-opens the scan root. Q-008 recorded about 21 s for a dead TCP endpoint. Validation cut only loopback shares (67) and a mapped letter (3), so a Wi-Fi-off, server-asleep or tunnel-down cut in W-003 is unmeasured.

still unknown: On the person's own C:\, how many of core.foldersVanished are renames or moves (installers, updaters) and how many are deletions? The Sandbox C:\ had 8 vanished folders, 3 from Windows itself, and nothing separates them. The answer decides whether N-055/N-056 become work.

still unknown: Does W-001 -Stopped now end 'held' on a busy C:\? Q-016 assumed taking gone folders out of the unreadable record fixes OtherCodeDiffers (Compare-StoppedRows, WindowCases.ps1:6645-6667). Validation did not run W-001, and a stopped run leaves a not-yet-reached folder NotListed while the finished run counts it as a listed empty folder.
still unknown: Why does a FAT32 or exFAT root fail with 87, and is it specific to the Sandbox's vdisk volumes? No real removable drive was tried, and plugging one in is a physical act for the person.

went wrong: Five gates ran twice and none of the second runs was a fix of bad work. Build-check halted on a 'partial' survey whose only 'present' row was the regression guard, then 'built anyway'. Design halted on its own 'irreversible' label for adding the core.foldersVanished key to WindowReport schema 1, which is additive. Critique and code-review halted for findings awaiting disposal. Validate halted on O-002, which could not be measured on this machine and was waived as N-058 right after. That is about five lost laps.

went wrong: The design cited four E007* test classes that do not exist in 4 of its 14 cases. This is the third slice with the same gap (lessons #876, #888, #896). Critique M2 caught it, but the design was written without those lessons and the builder replaced the checks.

went wrong: The design filed the 2/3-means-gone precondition only as a person check (SMB, DFS, ReFS, FAT). The volume-loss half was measurable here with a SUBST letter, and the critique found it as a major. It grew the slice by a root-open check, a shared SubstDrive helper with a lock, VolumeLossCorpus.json and 15 obligations.

went wrong: The regex spelling family was declared closed (O-017, 38-row corpus) and reopened by the code review with `case 2 or 3:`, `case (2 or 3):` and `2 or 3 =>` arms. The two code-review readers filed the same two findings separately (m1/IN-m1, m2/IN-m2). Each pair became its own waived obligation, and SC-080 and SC-081 are duplicates on the backlog.

went wrong: Triage marked the 'deleted or moved' wording fix for m2 and IN-m2 accepted-pending, as cheap and required. The obligations then waived O-019 and O-021 as 'a miss nobody required', so the shipped note still says 'deleted'. The ScanResult.FoldersVanished doc ('so it was the folder that was deleted', ScanResult.cs:191-193) is not among the files the comment-fix commit 5809f30c7 touched (Scanner.cs, SubstDrive.cs, the repro test), so it likely still says so.

went wrong: The first code-review lap read 10 of 18 changed files only partly or not at all. The repro test was never opened. WindowReport.cs, MainWindow.xaml.cs and ScanResult.cs were read through diff hunks only. Its two real findings came from scratch probes, not from reading the App-side changes.

went wrong: Validation could not reach the person's own C:\, the window script's Cases A and B on this desktop, throw mode (exit 70) or FAT/exFAT. The live-C:\ evidence is from a Sandbox on build 10.0.26100, and this PC runs 26300.

went wrong: The same Scanner.Scan probe was rewritten about six times (investigation, survey, three spikes, validation). Three spikes also deviated from the method's repo path and hit NU1301 on a mixed local-and-URL restore.
